title: Fix Wgpu Window Options Chip Z-Order
description: Fix folded Window Options and Command chip buttons in the wgpu renderer so they render below glassy side panels. Root cause: folded chips are drawn to the overlay draw list backdrop tier, which composites on top of side panel glass. Fix: render chips to the main draw list instead, matching unfolded rails.
summary:
The prior fix (routing folded chip/rail glass to the main draw list) had been undone by a later `with_chrome_sink` refactor: `render_window_measures_rail` and `render_window_engagement_rail` (framework/renderer/wgpu/rs/lib.rs) wrapped their entire bodies — both the folded chip AND the unfolded rail — in `with_chrome_sink(draw, overlay, ...)`, which redirects painting to the `overlay` draw list whenever an overlay is present (i.e. whenever side panels are open). Since `composite_to_swapchain` (ui/wgpu/rs/lib.rs) composites the `overlay` list's glass/content entirely after the main `draw` list, and side panels also paint to `overlay`, both the folded chip and the open rail ended up compositing above glassy side panels regardless of push order.

Fix: both functions now paint unconditionally to the main `draw` list (bypassing `with_chrome_sink`), while still threading the real `overlay` slot through to nested content (e.g. dropdown selects inside the measures rail) so those still layer correctly. This matches how side panels stay on `overlay` and composite after `draw`.

Verified: `cargo check`/`cargo test -p semio-framework-renderer-wgpu --lib` clean, no regressions (same pre-existing 4 dock-layout test failures unrelated to this change, tracked separately). Live pixel verification was attempted in the `flow` playground under wgpu (isolated dev server, plugin loaded correctly, `navigator.gpu.requestAdapter()` succeeded, canvas + WebGPU context created, boot completed with zero console errors) but the canvas never presented visible pixels in this headless Browser pane — a non-DOM screenshot sanity check (example.com) confirmed the screenshot pipeline itself works, so this is the environment's headless-WebGPU rendering gap documented in `.repo/🎫️/26/07/04/RUST-PLUGIN-FRAMEWORK-MIGRATION/parity-gap-update.md`, not a code issue. Closing on the strength of the structural fix (traced against composite_to_swapchain's actual compositing order) plus clean compile/tests; pixel-level confirmation needs a real (non-headless) browser.
